text:
Raphael Lavoie waited a long time for this one. Drafted 38th overall by the Oilers in 2019, he put up 25 goals in 61 AHL games for Bakersfield in 2022-23, and on Tuesday at T-Mobile Arena he scored his first NHL goal, a wrist shot at 8:01 of the third period that put VGK ahead 2-1. It was the goal that broke open a tie game, and it helped the Golden Knights snap a three-game winless run (0-2-1) with a 4-1 win over OTT.

The score looks more comfortable than the game felt for most of it. OTT had more shot attempts, 68 to 57, and Shane Pinto's power-play goal 34 seconds into the third had made it 1-1. But the quality of chances, which is what expected goals measures, favored VGK 4.27 to 2.58, and our simulation of every shot gave VGK a 59% chance to win, so the result was fair but not lopsided. Adin Hill was the quiet difference: he stopped 25 of 26 shots and saved about 1.6 goals more than the chances against him should have allowed, with Jonas Johansson holding OTT in it at the other end until late.

Karlsson made it 3-1 at 18:00, and Jack Eichel added a backhand with seven seconds left. Braeden Bowman, who came up as an undrafted free agent through Henderson, scored the opener on the power play, and Nic Dowd reached 200 career points with an assist on Lavoie's goal. VGK leaves with its winless run over and a night to remember for a first-time scorer. OTT goes home having outshot a team it couldn't beat.
